source.title: Understanding and inverse design of implicit bias in stochastic learning: a geometric perspective
source.authors: Nicola Aladrah; Emanuele Ballarin; Matteo Biagetti; Alessio Ansuini; A. d'Onofrio; Fabio Anselmi

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses implicit bias as a tool to design a parametrization, then evaluates binary-weight recovery in a synthetic Ising task. It does not test any mapped version about generalization or the training–test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports binary-coupling recovery and train/test prediction-MSE curves, but neither is a result on the mapped claim versions. The prediction-MSE curves are figure-only; numerical values are not stated.
record.test_reason: The study develops and tests a designed preference for binary weights in synthetic Ising regression. It neither tests nor uses any specific V1–V8 finding as a tool. General discussion of implicit bias and possible generalization benefits does not establish a test of these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their holomorphic construction reproduces a preference for binary weights comparable to a tuned explicit regularizer in a controlled Ising experiment, supporting their inverse-design mechanism. Broader implications for generalization remain prospective.
record.recipe_differences: The study designs a holomorphic parametrization and tests binary interaction recovery on synthetic Ising data; it does not reproduce the original studies’ natural-label generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The parametrized model uses resampled Gaussian target noise; all three methods use batch size 1. Hyperparameters were tuned separately for each method.

fits_no_version.finding: The parametrized and explicitly regularized methods achieve coupling reconstruction errors of (3.8 ± 2.1) × 10−16 and (2.4 ± 0.1) × 10−12; vanilla regression achieves 892.96 with standard deviation below 0.01.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this tuned synthetic Ising recovery experiment, a binary-favoring holomorphic parametrization achieves near-exact coupling recovery comparable to explicit double-well regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2(b) compares training and held-out prediction MSE across the three methods, without numerical curve values stated in the prose.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Designed parametrization and explicit regularization can be compared with vanilla regression on prediction error for unseen spin configurations.

record.problems: The experiment is a controlled synthetic Ising recovery task, not a natural-label classification task. The training/test prediction-MSE comparisons are presented as plots without numerical values in the text. The parameter trajectories are reported as consistent with the proposed dynamics, while the stated attraction conditions are theoretical assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were found. Figure 2 also shows charge diagnostics and learned-weight distributions, which concern the designed mechanism rather than the mapped claim versions.

untested.parts: Coexistence of fixed random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the same architecture and training recipe. Resampled Gaussian energy-target noise is not a fixed random-label experiment.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning; all experimental methods here use SGD.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations; batch size is fixed at one.
Dropout effects on held-out error and their dependence on data size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and measuring test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts apply to V1–V8. Near-exact coupling recovery and held-out regression curves alone do not test those specific claims. The parametrized method additionally uses resampled target noise, and hyperparameters are selected using ground-truth coupling reconstruction error.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and their tuning or regularization conditions.
Large-batch training and adaptations to its generalization gap.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Parametrized model
rows.operation_detail: Trained the binary parametrization on Ising energy observations; report coupling reconstruction error across ten runs.
rows.note: A synthetic binary-weight reconstruction result; it does not measure a mapped generalization claim version.
rows.check: The reported reconstruction error is correct, but evaluates the study's own method outside V1–V8. The ten runs vary stochastic training seeds while keeping the interaction matrix, training data, and initialization fixed.

rows.subject: Regularized model
rows.operation_detail: Trained direct couplings with a double-well penalty favoring binary values; report coupling reconstruction error across ten runs.
rows.note: Explicitly regularized comparator in a synthetic reconstruction task.
rows.check: The reported reconstruction error is correct, but this explicitly regularized method comparison measures none of V1–V8. Runs share the interaction matrix, data, and initialization.

rows.check: The reported reconstruction error is correct, but direct linear regression on Ising energies measures none of V1–V8. Runs share the interaction matrix, data, and initialization.
